summary.name: OpenSSH
summary.one_liner: OpenSSH is a suite of encrypted remote login and file transfer tools implementing the SSH protocol, developed by OpenBSD Project developers.
summary.what_it_does: OpenSSH provides ssh, scp, and sftp for remote operations, encrypting traffic to prevent eavesdropping and connection hijacking. Key management is handled by ssh-add, ssh-keygen, ssh-keyscan, and ssh-keysign. The server side includes sshd, sftp-server, and ssh-agent. It also offers tunneling capabilities, several authentication methods, and configuration options. The page announces release 10.6 dated October 6, 2026.
notable: Encrypts all SSH traffic and provides secure tunneling
Includes ssh, scp, sftp client tools and sshd, sftp-server, ssh-agent server side
Developed by OpenBSD Project developers under a BSD-style license
Contributions go to the OpenBSD Foundation
caveats: Page does not list supported platforms explicitly
